title: Apply for a recreational fishing licence (1-year or 3-year)
summary: Find out when and how to apply for a recreational fishing licence for NSW waters.
intro:
A recreational fishing licence is required if you want to fish in NSW waters, both freshwater and saltwater.

You need a licence if:

Activities in NSW freshwater or saltwater that require a licence include:
who_can_apply: You must be fishing in NSW waters (freshwater or saltwater).
what_you_need: MyServiceNSW Account (to add a digital licence)
The Service NSW app (to add a digital licence)

how_to_steps.text: Select a licence duration, either 1 year or 3 years.
Enter the date you want your licence to start.
Select a type of licence, either a digital licence or plastic card.
Review your details and make sure they are correct before proceeding to payment.

fees:
The NSW Government recreational fishing licence fees are:

If you need a licence for a shorter time you can apply for a 3-day or 1-month licence.

You must show your licence fee receipt if asked by an authorised officer.

For more information on recreational fishing and licence fees visit NSW Primary Industries website.

### Fee exemptions

Not everyone has to pay a fee for a recreational fishing licence.

Check if you are eligible for a recreational fishing fee exemption.

If you are eligible, you'll need to carry the necessary proof with you when you're fishing, in case you're called upon to show it.

faqs.q: Do I need a licence to fish in NSW?
faqs.a: Yes, a recreational fishing licence is required if you want to fish in NSW waters, both freshwater and saltwater.

faqs.q: What are the different licence options?
faqs.a: You can apply for a 1-year or 3-year licence, or you can apply for a 3-day or 1-month licence for shorter periods.

faqs.q: How do I apply for a licence?
faqs.a: Select the 'Apply online' button, choose a duration (1 year or 3 years), enter the start date, select a licence type (digital or plastic card), enter your personal details, and review your information before paying.
Not everyone has to pay a fee. You should check if you are eligible for a recreational fishing fee exemption.
